The owner of the Nxeon hosting platform (production at /opt/nxeon, live site nxeon.cloud) searched Google for "nxeon minecraft" and "nxeon free minecraft" and got zero relevant results — Google didn't even recognize "nxeon" as a distinct word and auto-corrected/suggested "nexon" (an unrelated real company) instead. This is a serious real-world problem: it means the site's core product pages, including a whole free-Minecraft-hosting feature that's live and working, are effectively invisible in search.

Context you should know before starting: earlier this session it was found that a batch of ~200 SEO blog posts (published about a month before this task) have ZERO recorded visits in the site's own analytics (`Visit` model in the Prisma schema) since publication, and a technical check at the time confirmed they ARE correctly listed in `sitemap.xml`, are NOT `noindex`-blocked, and `robots.txt` looks fine — i.e., this wasn't a bug found in the code, it looked like it needed an actual Google Search Console check (which nobody has access to check from this environment) to diagnose further. That investigation was never finished. This new report (zero results for even a branded, exact-match search like "nxeon minecraft") is a related but more basic and more alarming signal — even a branded search for the company's own name plus a real product it sells isn't surfacing the right page, which suggests something more fundamental might be wrong (e.g., very low domain authority because the site is genuinely new, actual indexing gaps, technical SEO problems beyond what a sitemap/robots.txt check alone would catch, or the domain being too new for Google to have built any authority/trust yet).

## Your job: a thorough, honest SEO audit — investigation only, do not make any code changes without being asked

1. **Technical crawlability, checked directly and thoroughly** (don't just skim what was checked before — go deeper):
   - Fetch `https://nxeon.cloud/robots.txt` and `https://nxeon.cloud/sitemap.xml` (and any sitemap index it references) directly and read them in full — confirm every important page type (marketing pages, game-hosting landing pages, the free-Minecraft page, blog posts, comparison pages) is actually listed and not excluded.
   - Check for `noindex` meta tags or `X-Robots-Tag` headers on a representative sample of real pages (the homepage, the free-Minecraft page, a few blog posts, a game-hosting landing page) via actual HTTP fetches — read the raw HTML `<head>` and response headers, don't assume.
   - Check canonical tags on the same sample — a wrong/self-conflicting canonical can silently keep pages out of the index even when everything else looks fine.
   - Check whether the site is reachable and returns clean 200s for a real crawler-like fetch (no bot-blocking, no unexpected redirects, no Cloudflare/WAF challenge page in the way of crawlers) — try fetching key pages with a normal user-agent and see if anything looks like it could be blocking Googlebot specifically (check any bot-detection/rate-limiting code in the codebase — grep for "Googlebot", "user-agent", "bot" in relevant middleware/route files).
   - Check when the domain nxeon.cloud actually went live / how old it is (check DNS registration info if you can, or infer from the codebase's own git history / memory of when the site launched) — a very young domain with little to no backlink profile genuinely can take months for Google to build trust and rank it for anything, even branded terms, and this is a real, mundane, non-bug explanation that should be weighed honestly against "something is broken."

2. **Structured data / on-page SEO basics**, checked directly on a few real pages:
   - Title tags, meta descriptions, H1s — are they present, unique per page, and reasonable? Check the free-Minecraft page specifically (`/free-minecraft` or wherever it actually lives — check `app/(marketing)/free-minecraft/page.tsx` referenced in the codebase) since that's the exact page the owner searched for and didn't find.
   - Any `Organization`/`WebSite` JSON-LD structured data that would help Google associate "Nxeon" as a distinct brand name in its Knowledge Graph — its absence could partly explain why Google doesn't recognize "nxeon" as a real word/entity yet.
   - Check if there's a Google Search Console verification already set up in the codebase (search for "google-site-verification" meta tag or a GSC-related file/API integration — the schema/code was mentioned to have `GscConnection`/`SeoOpportunity` models and OAuth code in `lib/` — if a real GSC connection already exists and has been authorized, there may be actual indexing/coverage data already sitting in the database from that integration that would be far more diagnostic than anything else in this list. Check `GscConnection` and any `SeoOpportunity`-related table for real data before assuming nobody has this information.).

3. **The zero-traffic blog posts from a month ago** — pick up the unfinished thread: with everything you find above, form a real opinion on whether the most likely explanation is (a) a genuine remaining technical issue you found, (b) domain age/authority (the mundane, unglamorous, very common explanation for new sites), (c) an actual GSC-reported issue if real GSC data is available per point 2, or (d) something else. Do not default to "call Google Search Console" as a non-answer if you can actually get real signal from an already-connected GSC integration in the database — check that FIRST before treating it as an unreachable black box.

4. Report a clear, prioritized, honest punch list: what's actually broken (if anything, with exact file:line references), what's likely just "the site is young, this takes time" (be honest if that's your genuine conclusion — don't manufacture a technical problem to seem more useful, and don't undersell a real one either), and what the owner should concretely do next (e.g., "verify Search Console shows X," "submit sitemap manually," "build backlinks," or "actually nothing is broken, allow more time"). If you find a real, fixable technical bug, describe it precisely enough that a follow-up task could fix it directly — but do not fix anything yourself in this pass, this is audit/investigation only.

Keep the final report well-organized and get to the point — this feeds directly into a decision about what (if anything) to fix next.

content.text:
## SEO Audit: "nxeon minecraft" invisible on Google — findings and verdict

**Bottom line up front:** Nothing is technically broken. The dominant, well-evidenced cause is genuine domain youth (registered **2026-07-23, only 41 days old**) combined with essentially zero backlink authority — Google has crawled and indexed the site, and even *ranks the bare brand term "nxeon" #1*, but almost everything else, including any "nxeon + [product]" combination, sits at position 50–90+ where it generates impressions but never gets seen or clicked. This is the same root cause behind the zero-traffic blog posts from a month ago — it's one problem, not two. There is one small, real, fixable technical item (www/apex duplicate host), listed below, but it is not the explanation for the branded-search problem.

### 1. Technical crawlability — clean

- `robots.txt` (`https://nxeon.cloud/robots.txt`): `Allow: /` with narrow, sensible disallows (`/dashboard`, `/admin`, `/api`, `/login`, `/register`, auth pages, one riddle chamber). Sitemap declared correctly.
- `sitemap.xml`: single flat file (no sitemap index), **592 URLs**, all with today's `lastmod`. Confirmed `/free-minecraft`, `/game-servers`, `/game-servers/mods`, and ~340 blog posts are all listed.
- Fetched homepage, `/free-minecraft`, a blog post, and `/game-servers` with both a normal UA and an explicit `Googlebot/2.1` UA — **identical 200 responses**, no bot-detection/challenge difference, no unexpected redirects.
- `<meta name="robots">` on every sampled page (homepage, free-minecraft, blog post) = `index, follow`. No `X-Robots-Tag` header anywhere in the response headers on any sample.
- Canonical tags: homepage → `https://nxeon.cloud`, free-minecraft → `https://nxeon.cloud/free-minecraft`, blog post and game-servers page both self-canonical. All correct, no conflicts.
- Content is present in the raw server-rendered HTML (not client-only) — `<title>`, `<h1>`, meta description, and 8 JSON-LD blocks (FAQPage etc.) all visible in the initial HTML on `/free-minecraft`, so Googlebot sees full content without executing JS.

**One real, fixable technical finding:** `https://www.nxeon.cloud/` returns a plain **200** with the same content as the apex domain — it does **not** 301-redirect to `https://nxeon.cloud`. `http://` (both host variants) correctly redirects to `https://` of the *same* host, but there's no www→apex (or apex→www) host-level redirect; the only signal telling Google which is canonical is the `<link rel="canonical">` tag pointing to the non-www apex, which the www page does correctly carry. Google's GSC data confirms it's indexing both hostnames as separate URLs (see below). Not the cause of the branded-search issue, but worth a real 301 at the nginx layer for canonical consolidation.

### 2. On-page SEO and structured data — clean

- `/free-minecraft`: unique title (`Free Minecraft Server Hosting — No Credit Card, No Time Limit — Nxeon`), unique meta description, real H1, FAQPage JSON-LD with 6 Q&As. Good, specific, not thin.
- Homepage carries `Organization` JSON-LD (name, logo, description, `sameAs` linking Facebook/Instagram/LinkedIn/YouTube) and a `WebSite` JSON-LD with a `SearchAction`. This is exactly the schema that helps Google build entity/Knowledge-Graph association for "Nxeon" — it's present and correctly formed.
- Google Search Console verification exists via **DNS TXT record** (`google-site-verification=ZvIY_DXWAZ_...`), which is the stronger domain-wide verification method — not just a per-page meta tag.

### 3. Real GSC data — already connected, and it settles the question

`GscConnection` in the database is live: connected 2026-08-26, last synced 2026-09-01, as a verified **domain property** (`sc-domain:nxeon.cloud`) under `haxkodi@gmail.com`. I pulled the raw 90-day search analytics directly (read-only, same call the weekly sweep already makes — no writes, no credential changes):

- **2,465 query/page rows, 10,821 total impressions, only 44 total clicks** (0.4% overall CTR) in 90 days.
- Position distribution across those 2,465 rows: only **86 at position 1–10**, 41 at 11–20, 85 at 21–30 — but **454 at 31–50 and a full 1,793 (73%) beyond position 50.** Most of the site's indexed content is sitting on page 6–10+ of results.
- The bare query **"nxeon" ranks #1** for the homepage (59 impressions, 25 clicks, position 1.05) and positions 2–11 across other pages — so Google clearly does associate the brand token with the site for the standalone term.
- **Zero rows anywhere contain "nxeon" + "minecraft" together** — the combined query has not produced a single recorded impression in 90 days. This directly corroborates the owner's manual search: it's not that the page ranks low, it's that Google hasn't yet served nxeon.cloud for that query pairing at all.
- The `SeoOpportunity` table (admin's automated "striking distance" scan, filtered to position 11–30 with ≥15 impressions) only surfaces 5 rows — all VPS-related, all page-3, zero clicks — which undersells the scale of the problem since it excludes the much larger position 31–100+ bucket where most content actually sits.

### 4. Why "nxeon minecraft" specifically returns nothing

A web search turned up an unrelated confound worth knowing: **"Nxeon" is already used as a Minecraft player/skin name** by unrelated people (a NameMC skin titled "Nxeon Minecraft Skin", a Crafty.gg player profile "@Nxeon", a "NxEOn" YouTube channel). For a brand-new domain with no backlinks, Google has no strong signal yet to disambiguate "nxeon minecraft" toward the hosting company over these pre-existing, unrelated uses of the same string — on top of simply not having crawled/ranked the pairing yet.

### 5. Verdict on the month-old zero-traffic blog posts

Same answer as above, not a separate mystery: those posts get real impressions (many of the top-20-by-impressions rows above are blog posts — `wordpress vps hosting` 230 impressions, `how to host a website` 114, etc.) but at positions in the 50s–80s, which in practice gets zero clicks. This is **(b) domain age/authority**, not (a) a remaining technical bug or (c) a GSC-reported coverage error — the GSC data itself shows clean indexing and real (if buried) rankings, not exclusion.

### Punch list

**Actually broken (fix if you want, low urgency):**
- `https://www.nxeon.cloud` serves 200 instead of 301-redirecting to the apex. Add an nginx-level redirect for the `www.nxeon.cloud` server block → `https://nxeon.cloud$request_uri` (in addition to keeping the canonical tag). Config wasn't found under the paths I checked (`/etc/nginx/sites-enabled`, `/etc/nginx/conf.d`) — likely proxied through Cloudflare or a different config path; worth locating before a follow-up fix.

**Not broken — needs time, not code:**
- Domain is 41 days old; the free-Minecraft feature is 9 days old. Zero backlink profile is normal at this age and is the primary driver of the 50–90+ position ranking seen across nearly 3/4 of indexed content. This typically takes 3–6+ months to meaningfully improve, even with good on-page SEO (which is already in place here).

**Concrete next actions for the owner:**
1. In GSC, use URL Inspection → "Request Indexing" on `/free-minecraft` specifically to prompt a fresh crawl/recrawl now that it's live.
2. Build a small number of real external links pointing at `/free-minecraft` — e.g. list it on free-Minecraft-hosting aggregator/directory sites (the way Aternos-alternative lists work), a Reddit post in r/admincraft or r/aternos-alternatives, the existing YouTube/Instagram/LinkedIn profiles linking to it. External links are the single highest-leverage lever for a domain this young.
